gap_notes: No Layer 2 sign objects yet. motivation / strengths / excess / deficiency / behavioral_tendencies are not 'wrong'; they belong to a later interpretive layer and wait for matching loci. Opened classical divisions (Ptolemy I.14–I.15, I.21; Lilly CA I.16) do not attest them. Do not invent 12 sign objects.

Element conflict: Lilly assigns fire/earth/air/water triplicities. Ptolemy I.21 groups the same four triangles but by winds/directions and planetary lords, not Aristotelian elements on the signs. Do not treat Ptolemy as attesting Aries=fire.

Mode conflict: schema has cardinal|fixed|mutable. Lilly names Aries/Cancer/Libra/Capricorn moveable and cardinal. Ptolemy splits tropical (Cancer, Capricorn) from equinoctial (Aries, Libra). Schema cannot store that split; do not silently collapse Ptolemy into cardinal.
Ptolemy I.15 dismisses quadrupedal/terrestrial/fruitful labels as unimportant. Lilly CA I.16 uses them (e.g. significator in Aries: rash, hardy, lascivious). Not compared.
Lilly CA I.16 nature/quality of all twelve signs is now opened. Diseases/places/kingdoms/corporature remain horary accidentalia. Layer 2 objects still withheld (required psych slots unattested).
CORE cannot be scored for sign meaning packages.

Commanding/obeying: Lilly's Aries–Virgo vs Libra–Pisces list matches Ptolemy I.17 summer/winter semicircle grouping (compared). Ptolemy also defines a pair-relation by equal distance from the equinox; Lilly's list does not attest that geometry. Do not collapse.

Ptolemy I.18 beholding/equal power (equal distance from a tropic) is not the same lemma as Lilly Antiscion (CA I.16 p.89–91). Lilly cites 'PTOL. APHO.' and adds Contrantiscion as square/opposition. Attribution is not consensus.
Lilly's Northern list in the same chapter says six signs but names five (Leo omitted in this scan). The commanding list on printed p.91 is complete; that is the compared grouping.
Lilly long/short ascension is rising-time technique, not Layer 2 meaning. Opened list puts Aquarius in both columns; not normalized.
Valens I.2 calls Aries fiery and also by nature watery (thunder/hail weather). Do not use Valens to confirm Lilly fire, and do not collapse weather into element.
Valens I.2 Aries is tropic. That is not Ptolemy equinoctial and not Lilly moveable/cardinal. Schema still cannot store the split; do not compare.
Valens I.3 (50 terms) is bounds/dignity, not Layer 2 meaning. Left in Foundation §2.5. Not copied here.

1.3.64: Houlding triplicity ontology ingested (trigonal geometry; elemental labels later; no Ptolemy air/water-on-sign). Rulers, Dorotheus fortune, dignity, and technique not copied. Do not CORE with Lilly fire. Do not materialize 12 sign objects. Later-interpretive slots still unattested.

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XIV (Ashmand p.23)
claims.original_claim: Aries is equinoctial: the first thirty degrees after the vernal equinox, when day and night are equal.
claims.normalized_claim: Aries is equinoctial, not merely 'cardinal' in Ptolemy's vocabulary

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Moveable (1659 p.87–88)
claims.original_claim: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn are moveable and cardinal; from the Sun's entry we name the quarters of the year.
claims.normalized_claim: Lilly classes Aries as moveable and cardinal

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XV (Ashmand p.23–24)
claims.original_claim: Signs alternate masculine-diurnal and feminine-nocturnal from Aries, which is masculine because the active principle takes precedence.
claims.normalized_claim: Aries is masculine and diurnal; signs then alternate

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Masculine (1659 p.87)
claims.original_claim: Masculine diurnal signs, therefore hot: Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, Aquarius; the others feminine nocturnal, therefore cold.
claims.normalized_claim: Aries is masculine and diurnal; signs then alternate

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XXI (Ashmand p.29–30)
claims.original_claim: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius form the first triplicity; lords Sun and Jupiter; principally northern by Jupiter's airy winds, also north-west by Mars.
claims.normalized_claim: Ptolemy's Aries-Leo-Sagittarius triangle is a wind/direction triplicity

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Elements (1659 p.87)
claims.original_claim: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius are fiery, hot and dry, and constitute the fiery triplicity.
claims.normalized_claim: Lilly's Aries-Leo-Sagittarius triangle is the fiery element

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XIV (Ashmand p.23)
claims.original_claim: Fixed signs immediately follow tropical and equinoctial signs; the season's quality is then more firmly established.
claims.normalized_claim: Fixed signs confirm the season begun in the preceding turning sign

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Fixed (1659 p.88)
claims.original_claim: Fixed signs follow the equinoctial and tropics: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; the season is then fixed.
claims.normalized_claim: Fixed signs confirm the season begun in the preceding turning sign

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XIV (Ashmand p.23)
claims.original_claim: Bicorporeal signs follow the fixed and participate in both the fixed and the tropical constitutions.
claims.normalized_claim: Bicorporeal/common signs partake of both neighbouring constitutions

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Common (1659 p.88)
claims.original_claim: Common signs sit between moveable and fixed: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces; they partake of both, and are bicorporeal.
claims.normalized_claim: Bicorporeal/common signs partake of both neighbouring constitutions

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XVII (Ashmand p.26)
claims.original_claim: The signs in the summer semicircle are commanding; those in the winter semicircle, obeying: when the Sun is in the former he makes the day longer than the night.
claims.normalized_claim: Summer-semicircle signs command; winter-semicircle signs obey

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Commanding (1659 p.91; djvu 117)
claims.original_claim: Signs commanding: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo. Signs obeying: Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces.
claims.normalized_claim: Summer-semicircle signs command; winter-semicircle signs obey

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XVII (Ashmand p.26)
claims.original_claim: Any two signs configurated at equal distance from the same or either equinoctial point are termed commanding and obeying: equal ascensional times and equal parallels.
claims.normalized_claim: Ptolemy's commanding/obeying is also a pair-relation by equal distance from the equinox

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XVIII (Ashmand p.26–27)
claims.original_claim: Any two signs equally distant from either tropical sign are equal in power; they also behold each other, rising and setting from the same parts of the horizon.
claims.normalized_claim: Ptolemy's beholding/equal-power signs are pairs equally distant from a tropic

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Antiscion (1659 p.89–91; djvu 114–117)
claims.original_claim: Antiscion signs are of the same virtue and equally distant from the first degree of Cancer or Capricorn. Contrantiscion is of the nature of a square or opposition.
claims.normalized_claim: Lilly's Antiscion is tropical-distance sympathy; Contrantiscion is classed with square/opposition

claims.author: Vettius Valens / Mark Riley trans.
claims.edition: Riley unperfected English; Kroll 1908 / Pingree 1986 Greek
claims.locus: Anthologies Book I ch.2 Nature of the Twelve Zodiacal Signs (Aries)
claims.original_claim: Aries is a masculine sign, tropic, terrestrial, governing, fiery.
claims.normalized_claim: Valens' Aries is masculine; diurnal alternation is not attested in this sentence

claims.author: Vettius Valens / Mark Riley trans.
claims.edition: Riley unperfected English; Kroll 1908 / Pingree 1986 Greek
claims.locus: Anthologies Book I ch.2 Nature of the Twelve Zodiacal Signs (Aries)
claims.original_claim: Aries is listed as fiery, and also said to be by nature watery, with thunder and hail.
claims.normalized_claim: Valens' Aries is both fiery as a sign label and watery as weather

claims.author: Vettius Valens / Mark Riley trans.
claims.edition: Riley unperfected English; Kroll 1908 / Pingree 1986 Greek
claims.locus: Anthologies Book I ch.2 Nature of the Twelve Zodiacal Signs (Aries)
claims.original_claim: Aries is tropic. From its first degree to the equinox it is stormy; the middle degrees are milder.
claims.normalized_claim: Valens classes Aries as tropic, not as schema-cardinal

claims.author: Deborah Houlding
claims.locus: The Classical Use of Triplicities, Trigonal relationship of signs
claims.original_claim: Houlding restates Manilius: a triangle inscribed in the zodiac marks trigonal signs, each pair separated by three intervening signs.
claims.normalized_claim: Triplicity is a trigonal grouping of signs, not an elemental nature of each sign

claims.author: Deborah Houlding
claims.locus: The Classical Use of Triplicities, Trigonal relationship of signs
claims.original_claim: Houlding: the association of triplicities with elements arose from that geometry but was not explicitly stated by Ptolemy and his contemporaries.
claims.normalized_claim: Elemental labels on triplicities are later than Ptolemy's trigonal grouping

claims.author: Deborah Houlding
claims.locus: The Classical Use of Triplicities, Trigonal relationship of signs
claims.original_claim: Houlding: there was no characterisation of Aquarius as an air-sign or Scorpio as a water-sign in that early usage.
claims.normalized_claim: Ptolemy-era usage does not label Aquarius air-sign or Scorpio water-sign
